notes.text: Sean Durzi is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Braden Schneider has taken his spot beside Marcus Pettersson. That pair has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 91:16 together, up from 45% with Durzi.
Glenn Gawdin was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside Eeli Tolvanen and Jaroslav Chmelař.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 26% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Filip Chytil is on injured reserve (shoulder injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Tom Willander is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Guillaume Brisebois has taken his spot beside Jamie Oleksiak.
Jacob Quillan was added to the roster on Oct 31 and has played beside Linus Karlsson and Drew O'Connor.
Max Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 4% last season.

VAN.head: The Canucks face a real test
VAN.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage, the Rangers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks can pull it off if they keep shots to a minimum.

NYR.head: The Rangers have a lot going for them
NYR.body: Even though Vancouver has home-ice advantage, the Rangers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks’ way back in is keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: Something has to change for the Canucks
paras: The Canucks are on a six-game losing streak, while the Rangers (11-8-1) beat Calgary 3-1 on Wednesday. The Rangers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in New York on Oct 11. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (12th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Rangers’ record (.575) is about what their chances are worth. The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.175) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .338, mostly because they’re 2-5 in one-goal games.
In their six-game skid, the Canucks have been outscored 25-13, including 14-8 at 5-on-5.

The Rangers lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest), get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Canucks pick their shots (lowest) and have had shaky goaltending (32nd). They also have a leaky penalty kill (32nd), so the Rangers’ power play (8th) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. Vancouver has allowed 4.50 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Adam Fox (2 G / 20 A / 22 P in 20 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, and Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 11 A / 20 P in 20 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Canucks, Elias Pettersson (#40) (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brock Boeser (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 20 GP) has a team-high seven goals.
Dylan Garand (6-7-1 / .906 SV% in 12 GS) will likely start for the Rangers, and Leevi Meriläinen (2-8-1 / .889 SV% in 12 GS) for Vancouver.
